sentences.text: No. - 261 of 2004 Appellant :- Kumari Kamini Thru Naresh Singh S/O Daan Singh
Respondent :- Smt. Shakuntala Devi And Anr Counsel for Appellant :- Rajendra Jaiswal Counsel for Respondent :- Rakesh Kumar Tewari,Jitendra Narain Mishra Hon'ble Jaspreet Singh,J.

1. Heard learned counsel for the appellant and Shri Jitendra Narain Mishra, learned counsel appearing for the insurance company.
2.

The claimant has filed the instant appeal under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the award dated 31.01.2004 passed in Claim Petition No.144 of 2000 whereby the claim petition has been dismissed.
3. Submission of the learned counsel for the appellant is that on 07.08.2001, the appellant at around 1.00 p.m. was walking on the Unnao Hardoi Road.

At that fateful day and time, the offending truck Kumari Kamini Thru Naresh Singh S/O Daan ... vs Smt. Shakuntala Devi And Anr on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99959157/
1 bearing number U.P. 80 AF 9942 which was coming from side of Safipur was being driven rashly and negligently and it hit the claimant as a result a femur bone of the right leg was fractured and she sustained other injuries as well.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The claimant was first taken to Uma Shanker Dixit Hospital at Unnao from where she was further taken to Blue H. M. Hospital at Kanpur.

entities.text: Uma Shanker Dixit Hospital at Unnao
entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Blue H. M. Hospital at Kanpur
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: She was treated at Banerji Nursing Home at Magarwara, Unnao and at Bindi Nursing Hospital at Kanpur.

The appellant sustained disability of 50% and for the said reasons, she claimed a sum of Rs.5,60,000/-
by means of claim petition filed before the Claims Tribunal under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
4. Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that various documents were filed including the disability certificate issued by the Chief Medical Officer, however, were ignored.

The evidence of P.W.1 and P.W.2 who clearly stated that the appellant had suffered injuries on account of rash and negligent driving by the truck has also been discarded and as such the Tribunal has committed an error while rejecting the claim petition, hence the appeal.

5. Shri Jitendra Narain Mishra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company, on the other hand,
submits that even though it was alleged that the appellant suffered injuries in a motor accident on 07.08.2001, but no medical documents for treatment, the surgery if any, x-ray plates or for medication were brought on record by the appellant and it is in absence of vital evidence which ought to have been filed but not placing it on record, the Tribunal was justified in dismissing the claim petition.
Even otherwise, even while filing the appeal, no material has been brought on record till date to establish that any injury arising out of the motor accident was suffered by the appellant.
In such circumstances, the appeal is also without merit and deserves to be dismissed.
6. The Court has considered the rival submissions and also perused the material on record.
7. Apparently, it is the case of the appellant that she suffered injuries in the motor accident which occurred on 07.08.2001.

Upon perusal of the record which has been placed before the Court relating to the proceedings before the Tribunal not a single prescription, document relating to admission or treatment of the appellant in the various hospitals as mentioned has been brought on record.
All what has been brought on record is the FIR, the copy of the chargesheet.
The photocopy has been brought on record bearing paper no. Ga 39 which relates to U.H.M. Hospital, Kanpur 8.

Be that as it may, the said document does not inspire confidence for the reason that the same is a photocopy in the first place even otherwise it does not refer to any treatment or the first aid given to the appellant which is said to have been provided at a different hospital.
There is no document placed on record by which it could be established that the appellant was first taken to Uma Shanker Dixit Hospital, Unnao.

There is no document which indicates that the appellant was treated at Baneji Nursing Home Magarwara, Unnao nor any document relating to Bindi Nursing Home at Kanpur.
9.
Be that as it may, in case if any person sufferers from fracture of the femur bone at least the x-ray plate should have been present.
No document relating to the medication administered or any surgery which may have been under gone by the appellant has been brought on record.

There is no Kumari Kamini Thru Naresh Singh S/O Daan ... vs Smt. Shakuntala Devi And Anr on 15 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/99959157/
2 document of any doctor indicating that the appellant was examined and diagnosed or having suffered the said injuries.

entities.text: Kumari Kamini Thru Naresh Singh S/O Daan ... vs Smt. Shakuntala Devi And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Merely by filing the copy of the FIR and chargesheet does not establish the accidental injuries or the treatment of the appellant.
The evidence on behalf of the appellant was led by her father and another alleged eye witness Udaiveer Singh.
10. It will be relevant to notice that the instant appeal arises out of a compensation claimed made in respect of injuries suffered.
In such a circumstance, it was prime important for the appellant to have entered into the witness box and stated her version.
Significantly, she did not enter into the witness box to give any evidence.
If at all, the appellant had suffered such injuries the same could have easily been corroborated by medical evidence which is conspicuously absent.

The certificate filed on record issued by the Chief Medical Officer does not indicate that the said injury is the outcome of the accident since the said certificate is dated 29.10.2003 i.e. after two years from the alleged date of accident and there is nothing on record to connect that during these two years the appellant had suffered on account of accident and her treatment went on for two years.
11.

In view of the aforesaid, this Court is satisfied that the award passed by the claims Tribunal dated 21.01.2004 dismissing the Claim Petition No.114 of 2002 does not suffer from any error which may required the indulgence of this Court.
12. In view of the aforesaid, the appeal is dismissed.
Costs are made easy.
The record of the Tribunal be returned forthwith.
